To find the determinant of the 4×4 matrix, I'll expand along the first column since it contains two zeros.

The matrix is:
$$A = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 4 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 & 4 \\ 4 & 0 & -1 & 1 \\ 5 & 1 & -2 & -1 \end{pmatrix}$$

Expanding along column 1:
$$\det(A) = 0 \cdot C_{11} - 0 \cdot C_{21} + 4 \cdot C_{31} - 5 \cdot C_{41}$$

where $C_{ij} = (-1)^{i+j} M_{ij}$ are cofactors.

**Computing $C_{31}$:**
$$C_{31} = (-1)^{3+1} \begin{vmatrix} 4 & 3 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 4 \\ 1 & -2 & -1 \end{vmatrix} = (+1) \cdot M_{31}$$

Expanding this 3×3 determinant along the first row:
$$M_{31} = 4(1 \cdot (-1) - 4 \cdot (-2)) - 3((-1) \cdot (-1) - 4 \cdot 1) + 0$$
$$= 4(-1 + 8) - 3(1 - 4) = 4 \cdot 7 - 3 \cdot (-3) = 28 + 9 = 37$$

So $C_{31} = 37$.

**Computing $C_{41}$:**
$$C_{41} = (-1)^{4+1} \begin{vmatrix} 4 & 3 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = -M_{41}$$

Expanding along the first row:
$$M_{41} = 4(1 \cdot 1 - 4 \cdot (-1)) - 3((-1) \cdot 1 - 4 \cdot 0) + 0$$
$$= 4(1 + 4) - 3(-1) = 20 + 3 = 23$$

So $C_{41} = -23$.

**Final calculation:**
$$\det(A) = 0 - 0 + 4 \cdot 37 - 5 \cdot (-23) = 148 + 115 = 263$$
